Procedure vs In Re : Madhusudan Dolai on 22 August, 2017
Author: Joymalya Bagchi
Bench: Joymalya Bagchi
 1
22.08.2017
sdas C.R.R. No. 685 of 2017 In Re : An application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal
Procedure.

And In Re : Madhusudan Dolai ....... petitioner  Mr. Sourav Chatterjee  ....... for the petitioner  Mr. Saswata Gopal Mukherjee, learned P.P.,
 Mr. Ayan Basu  ...... for the State  Mr. Debabrata Roy,
 Mr. Bibekananda Tripathy  ....... for the opposite party no. 2 Let affidavit-of-service filed in Court be kept with record.

Order dated 23.09.2016 passed by the learned Additional District and Sessions Judge, Fast Track Court, Haldia, Purba Medinipur, in S.C.
No. 21(4) of 2016 refusing to discharge the petitioner from the aforesaid case has been assailed.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Fast Track Court, Haldia, Purba Medinipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Prosecution case against the petitioner is to the effect that the petitioner and other accused persons were dealing and/or selling spurious liquor and due to consumption of such liquor one Abhijit Manna and Amitava Karan expired.

In conclusion of investigation, charge- sheet was filed under Sections 272/273/328/304/120B of the Indian Penal Code, under Section 46AA of the Bengal Excise Act and 16(3) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act against the petitioner and other accused persons.
Learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that viscera report of the deceased Abhijit Manna showed that no poison was detected in the viscera of the deceased.

Relying on such report,
prayer was made to discharge the petitioner from the aforesaid case.
Such prayer being turned down the petitioner is before this Court.

Learned Counsel appearing for the State submits that opinion of the autopsy surgeon in the post-mortem report is that the victim Abhijit Manna had died due to unknown poisoning.

That apart, large quantity of illicit liquor was seized from the possession of the petitioner and other accused persons and chemical examination of seized liquor showed that it was spurious and unfit for human consumption.
Hence, the petitioner ought not to be discharged from the instant case.
I have considered the materials on record in the light of the rival submissions of the learned Counsels appearing for the parties.
Prima facie, there are materials to show that the petitioner and other accused persons were dealing in and/or selling spurious liquor which is unfit for human consumption.
There is also material on record to show that the victims who had consumed liquor at the shop of the petitioner had fallen sick and two of them subsequently died.
Opinion in the post-mortem report of Abhijit Manna disclosed that the death was due to poisoning.
However, final opinion was reserved upon receipt of viscera report.
It is true that the viscera report did not indicate poison in the viscera of the victim.
It is open to the prosecution to explain the reasons for absence of poison in the viscera report during the course of trial.

However, in view of overwhelming materials on record disclosing to involvement of the petitioner in dealing and/or selling of spurious liquor and the fact that number of persons who had consumed such liquor had been fallen sick and two of the victims had even died gives rise to a strong suspicion of involvement of the petitioner in the alleged offences and the trial court had rightly refused to discharge him from the instant case.

It is open to the petitioner to probabilise his defences in the course of trial which needless to mention shall be decided by the trial court independently on the basis of the evidence adduced without being swayed by the observations made in this order or in the order impugned.
Case diary be returned.
With the aforesaid observations, the application is disposed of.

Photostat certified copy of this order,
if applied for, shall be given to the parties as expeditiously as possible on compliance of all necessary formalities.

(Joymalya Bagchi, J.)
